rule: Route each sentence to the clearest original explanatory form: TraderCockpit-drawn deterministic mathematics for claims, draw-on or chalkboard motion for unfolding concepts, cards for definitions and comparisons, and trader-at-desk or real chart footage for human workflow. Supplied screenshots are reference-only and never appear verbatim. Generated atmosphere may bridge scenes but may never replace an available explanation or evidence asset.

search_multiplicity.test: selection bias from trying many candidates
search_multiplicity.geometry: full candidate field with the selected maximum highlighted only after every comparison is visible

holdout_sequencing.test: untouched later data and walk-forward evaluation
holdout_sequencing.geometry: chronological blocks with a frozen-rule boundary and moving train/test windows

population_distribution.geometry: all candidates as ordered marks, bars, or scatter points

threshold_fragility.test: near-miss density around a declared gate
threshold_fragility.geometry: measured points stay fixed while the threshold moves
forbidden_substitutes: red warning icon without a distribution

concentration_stress.test: dependence on a small number of contributors
concentration_stress.geometry: ranked contribution blocks removed one at a time

cost_sensitivity.geometry: same candidate field traced through declared cost levels and response curves

parameter_neighborhood.geometry: neighborhood heatmap or contour showing plateau versus isolated spike

monte_carlo_paths.test: path uncertainty under the declared perturbation mechanism
monte_carlo_paths.geometry: stored equity paths with terminal P&L color and neutral pointwise quantile bands

tail_resolution.test: Monte Carlo run-count error and lower-tail rank resolution
tail_resolution.geometry: inverse-square-root error curve plus ordered outcome dots

reproducibility.test: deterministic rerun under the same declared inputs

scene-01.treatment: Put the historical result on the left and the still-unanswered questions on the right. Never leave the definition of a backtest on a black screen.

scene-02.treatment: Animate a visible search history of tried versions before revealing the survivor count; do not jump straight to a single winner curve.

scene-03.treatment: Build the strategy checklist line by line: entry, exit, size, loss rule, costs, stop rule, and a reason that can fail.

scene-04.treatment: Place the winning-dollar and losing-dollar piles on screen, write the division, and move the ratio across the break-even line at one.

scene-05.treatment: Trace the running peak, the later trough, and the deepest peak-to-trough drop while the definition is spoken.

scene-06.treatment: Reveal each Golden Cross input from the separate historical test, then calculate profit factor and return-to-drawdown in view.

scene-07.treatment: Hold win rate beside average win, average loss, costs, and final arithmetic so no single percentage becomes the verdict.

scene-08.treatment: Count 1,335 entering and 184 surviving, then show overlapping gate failures with an explicit overlap label.

scene-09.treatment: Plot the failed profit factors around one, shade the declared ten-percent band, and keep the population-specific limitation visible.

scene-10.treatment: Move the threshold toward one while leaving every measured point fixed, making clear that a lower rule changes admission rather than performance.

scene-11.treatment: Carry the same 184 markers into the next screen instead of turning them into winner badges.

scene-12.treatment: Reveal earlier development prices, the frozen-rule boundary, and later untouched prices in chronological order; visibly relabel the holdout as used once it informs a revision.

scene-13.treatment: Close on the complete written process and the 184 candidates moving forward, not on an isolated green equity curve.

scene-hook.treatment: Animate many tried rules collapsing into one selected maximum, then move the untouched period into view.

scene-windows.treatment: Reveal development, warm-up, frozen-rule boundary, and holdout in order; show the search-count warning beside the development block.

scene-terminal.treatment: Use a point-in-time membership strip with delisted names remaining in their historical dates; do not use a generic terminal screen.

scene-gate.treatment: Count 184 entering, 154 positive-net, and 30 non-positive-net marks from the run-derived field.

scene-funnel.treatment: Keep the whole distribution visible while mean, median, and percentile ranks are introduced.

scene-distribution.treatment: Contrast a pre-specified result with the maximum selected after comparing 184 candidates.

scene-twins.treatment: Hold out-of-sample status constant while data quality, execution, dependence, regime coverage, and search count appear as separate unresolved dimensions.

scene-relief.treatment: Show the holdout changing into validation data the moment its result feeds a revision, followed by a new untouched block.

scene-406.treatment: Animate interval width shrinking continuously with sample size; do not draw a magical threshold at 100 trades.

scene-treasure.treatment: Remove the largest contributors one at a time and show how much of the reported result remains.

scene-limits.treatment: Advance rolling train/test windows through time, then expose the dependence caveat rather than calling the folds independent.

scene-diy.treatment: Build a plain-language test-plan checklist beside the locked timeline: dates, universe, costs, warm-up, search count, failures, distribution, and uncertainty.

scene-close.treatment: End on the untouched-data boundary, not a winner card.

scene-hook.treatment: Move every candidate from no-cost paper result to the cost-stressed field; never represent slippage with atmospheric darkness alone.

scene-stack.treatment: Separate commission, spread, market impact, and market movement before the fill as named cost components with units.

scene-formula.treatment: Write the fixed-ledger re-pricing equation on screen and label what was not re-simulated.

scene-numbers.treatment: Plot the actual 1x, 2x, and 3x stress outcomes and count failures at each level.

scene-elegant.treatment: Show why net-profit and profit-factor signs coincide on the same fixed trade ledger.

scene-stress.treatment: Keep every candidate response curve visible so slope and dispersion replace a single pass/fail card.

scene-bars.treatment: Animate the linear fixed-ledger deduction, then explicitly bracket the model conditions where linearity stops being credible.

scene-cliff.treatment: Use cliff as a descriptive shape only when the plotted response changes sharply; do not imply a universal theorem.

scene-casualty.treatment: Place market-order execution risk and limit-order non-fill/adverse-selection risk on the same trade-off diagram.

scene-survivor.treatment: Keep 2x and 3x as labeled scenario choices from this run, never as universal realistic-cost constants.

scene-count.treatment: Show per-side, round-trip, per-contract, and per-order units before multiplying cost by trade count.

scene-classes.treatment: Change spread, depth, volatility, size, order type, and urgency independently; avoid a one-size-fits-all asset-class badge.

scene-scar.treatment: Separate a wiring proof from external calibration and live-execution validation.

scene-diy.treatment: Build the cost-definition checklist from fill benchmarks, units, tested assumptions, and limitations.

scene-close.treatment: Close on measured sensitivity to cost assumptions, not on the word slippage floating over black.

scene-hook.treatment: Start with a response surface and identify stable plateaus versus narrow peaks.

scene-luck.treatment: Contrast one lucky point with the neighborhood and the full candidate field.

scene-mc.treatment: Define one Monte Carlo run and distinguish this parameter experiment from bootstrap resampling and Markov-chain Monte Carlo.

scene-what.treatment: Animate the exact selection probability and uniform plus-or-minus-thirty-percent multiplier while entry logic remains fixed.

scene-surface.treatment: Use the surface as a geometric explanation and label it illustrative unless its points come from stored run output.

scene-p05.treatment: Sort 200 values, mark the fifth-percentile rank convention, and show why nearby tail order statistics matter.

scene-misnamed.treatment: Display the implementation's misnamed field beside its actual lower-tail meaning; do not silently repeat the label.

scene-field.treatment: Plot all 46 entering candidates and the actual 18 pass/28 fail split.

scene-fan.treatment: Draw the 100 stored display paths with green profitable endings, red losing or flat endings, an explicit zero line, and neutral pointwise percentile bands. Never invent a losing path to balance the palette; keep the simultaneous-band limitation visible.

scene-casualty.treatment: Locate failures in the field and describe geometry without pretending a two-dimensional projection proves the cause.

scene-survivor.treatment: Separate passing this exact perturbation gate from universal robustness.

scene-determinism.treatment: Show seed derivation, repeat calculation, file-hash comparison, and software environment as distinct reproducibility checks.

scene-diy.treatment: Build the random-change recipe and reproducibility checklist before showing any result.

scene-limits.treatment: Plot the inverse-square-root error law and tail-event standard errors; never draw 200 as a maximum.

scene-close.treatment: Close on neighborhood stability plus a reproducible test record, not a simulation-count slogan.
